description: Executable evals for the code-clarity STANDARD in rules/code-clarity.md. This is a generative eval: it measures what the agent WRITES, not a gating speech-act. DESIGN (v2, after the greenfield v1 showed no discrimination): the greenfield single-function prompt could not flip because a strong base model already writes clean guard-clause code by habit (documented in the v1 REDGREEN.md). This v2 reproduces the REAL failure mechanism the original audit identified — Karpathy #3 ('match existing style even if you'd do it differently') pulling NEW code toward adjacent nested mess. Each eval primes the model with a deeply-nested example function 'from our codebase', then asks for a NEW sibling function with sequential preconditions, output-only so the discriminator sees just the new code. The rule text is the only variable: GREEN (rules/code-clarity.md present, whose 'new code follows this standard in full' + the CLAUDE.md #3 carve-out counteract the style-matching pull) vs RED (stripped via bin/redgreen.fish, leaving only Karpathy #3's raw 'match existing style'). If the fix works, the new sibling stays flat in GREEN and matches the nested staircase in RED. NOTE: a GREEN~=RED (no-flip) outcome remains a legitimate documented finding per rules-evals/REDGREEN-RUNBOOK.md, not a suite bug — do not manufacture a flip.
_contract_note: Assertions are regex-on-generated-code, not tool/skill-surface pins — the harness has no LLM-judge assertion type, so code structure is measured structurally. The load-bearing discriminator in each eval is the not_regex for deep indentation (>=10 leading whitespace chars = >=5 nesting levels at 2-space indent), PAIRED with a positive required assertion that proves real code was emitted (silent-fire trap closure). Two design guards vs the retired v1: (1) the new function is pure-conditional with no traversal, so deep indentation is unambiguously the anti-pattern rather than an honest nested loop; (2) 'output only the new function' isolates the discriminator to new code, not the primed nested example. Caveat recorded in REDGREEN.md: if a transcript shows the model echoing the nested example despite the instruction, the discriminator is contaminated for that run and the run is excluded.

evals.name: guard-clauses-new-sibling-in-nested-file
evals.summary: Primes the model with a 6-level nested canAccess 'from our codebase', then asks for a new sibling canRefund with six sequential preconditions. Tests whether the clarity standard stops the new code from matching the nested house style (the exact Karpathy #3 contradiction the fix targets).

assertions.description: Proves a real canRefund implementation was emitted (not planning-only output). Paired with the deep-nesting not_regex below so the discriminating negative assertion has actual code to judge — closes the silent-fire trap. Non-discriminating by design; its job is to gate the negative assertion.

DISCRIMINATOR. No emitted line is indented >=10 whitespace chars — at 2-space indent that is >=5 nesting levels, i.e. the arrow anti-pattern the standard forbids. Because the prompt says 'output only the new function' and the new function is PURE CONDITIONAL LOGIC (no data-structure traversal that legitimately needs loops), any line at >=10 spaces is unambiguously a nested staircase, not honest structure — this fixes the false-positive the retired extract-nested-loop eval had on a clean triple-traversal. GREEN (rule present) should keep the new sibling flat via guard clauses; RED (rule stripped) should trip IF the base model matches the deeply-nested example's style (Karpathy #3 pull). Limitation: assumes space indentation (tabs under-count) — documented in REDGREEN.md. Also assumes the model honors 'output only the new function' and does not echo the nested example; a first-result check confirms this before trusting the matrix.

[diagnostic] Invert-and-return-early signature — a negated guard condition (e.g. `if (!user) return false`). Guard-clause style inverts each exceptional case and returns; the nested style writes the positive `if (user) { ... }` and never negates. Diagnostic, not gating: a partial refactor may mix one negated guard with residual nesting.
